raw_record.question_text: In the figure, $\triangle ABC$ is isosceles, $\triangle DCE$ is equilateral, and $\triangle FCG$ is isosceles. Find the measure of $\angle 4$ at vertex $C$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: A, D, F, G, E, B lie on one straight horizontal line, C is the common top vertex, angle 4 is the angle between CG and CE, and the 77° label at F is the interior angle ∠CFG of triangle FCG. From the text, use that triangle FCG is isosceles with base FG as drawn, so ∠FGC = ∠CFG = 77°. Since G, E, and F are collinear, the angle inside triangle CGE at G is supplementary to 77°, so ∠CGE = 103°. From the text, triangle DCE is equilateral, and from the image EG lies along ED, so ∠CEG = 60°. Then in triangle CGE, angle 4 is 180° - 103° - 60° = 17°.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: D, F, G, E are on the same base line, C is the apex, angle 3 is ∠FCG, and angle 4 is the gap between CG and CE inside the larger equilateral triangle DCE. From the text, triangle FCG is isosceles with base FG as drawn, so the two base angles at F and G are equal; with the image label ∠CFG = 77°, the apex angle is angle 3 = 180° - 77° - 77° = 26°. Also from the text, triangle DCE is equilateral, so ∠DCE = angle 2 + angle 3 + angle 4 = 60°. Hence angle 2 + angle 4 = 60° - 26° = 34°, giving angle 4 = 17°.
